states.missing: the key is not set: the built-in default 0 applies, which means no ceiling — transcripts created or last written by a desktop-host surface (Claude Desktop, Cowork) are kept until deleted some other way. This default is unbounded retention and is NOT the cleanupPeriodDays default of 30 days; those transcripts are exempt from that sweep by default. Requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later.
states.zero: an explicit 0 is allowed (the key bounds an exemption from deletion; it never disables writes) and also means no ceiling.
states.positive_int: a hard ceiling in days for desktop-hosted transcripts; the effective retention is the longer of this ceiling and the effective cleanupPeriodDays.

retention_probes.managed_override: a managed source that sets cleanupPeriodDays makes this key ignored entirely, so a probe report must show which source governed the effective value (user settings vs managed policy), never just the number.
retention_probes.notes: Read only the stores the runtime itself consults: the User settings file and managed policy files. Never look under the desktop app's Application Support tree for this key — measured locally on 2026-10-16 (two machines, read-only), no retention key lives there. A one-run --settings flag also feeds the runtime but is per-session and invisible on disk; its absence from a disk probe is expected, not a gap.

harnesses.notes: Kimi Code (Moonshot AI CLI). Home directory: $KIMI_CODE_HOME when set, otherwise ~/.kimi-code; sessions live under <home>/sessions/<workspaceId>/, one directory per session, named by the session id itself (session_<uuid>). The transcript is agents/<agentId>/wire.jsonl inside that directory, main agent = agents/main/wire.jsonl. The filename is a constant, so the scanner cannot take the session id from it: this cell declares session_dir instead, which takes the id from the directory name and accepts only the declared relative file path. <home>/session_index.jsonl is a one-line-per-session index (sessionId, sessionDir, workDir) whose sessionId and workDir columns the scanner reads — the workDir is the session's observed working directory — and <home>/workspaces.json maps workspaceId -> project root and is not read. Both that working directory and the workspaceId segment above the session directory are read relative to the sessions root (<home>/sessions): a harness_roots override pointing at <home> itself or at a session directory leaves both dimensions unobserved. On-disk retention/cleanup: not established (no retention or sweep constant was found in the implementation that was read, so this stays unknown rather than 'none').
harnesses.seal_source: installed Kimi Code 0.39.1 implementation read 2026-09-19: the wire.jsonl writer is JournalWriter.append(scope, key, data), which per call does mkdir -> open(filePath, 'a') -> fh.writeFile(data) -> fh.sync() -> fh.close() in a finally block. No file descriptor is held across calls, so a later append reopens the path and a rename cannot strand it (same evidence class as the gemini-cli cell). The file's own comment states that append-only paths such as wire.jsonl use exactly this append path, not the atomic temp-file+rename writer used for whole-file writes.

harnesses.notes: DeepSeek Harness (dsh), an open-source agent harness. Every surface writes into one home: the desktop app, dsh web, headless, sdk and acp all use $DSH_HOME/sessions, so a session cannot be attributed to a surface and the registry declares no supported dimension. DSH_HOME replaces the home directory (default ~/.dsh), so the cells keep the /sessions/ suffix. The transcript is a concatenation of Zstandard frames whose first frame is the session header. The file name is a constant, so session_dir takes the id from the directory: a bare <uuid> for a subagent child, session-<uuid> otherwise. The <slug-of-cwd> component is lossy and must never be parsed; the header's cwd is authoritative. session.lock is 0 bytes and proves nothing about quiescence. Attachments live outside the log at <DSH_HOME>/attachments/v1 and are not archived yet.

harnesses.notes: Codebuff (formerly Manicode) CLI and its free/sponsored freebuff flavour: one product, one on-disk layout, legacy directory name manicode, three channel roots (prod, -dev, -staging) that are builds of the same tool and never surfaces. The native id is <project-basename>.<chat-id>, composed from the session directory path: the chat id IS the session start time in ISO-8601 with ':' -> '-', so the id's trailing component is a millisecond timestamp, not a UUID, and the basename keeps same-timestamp chats under different project basenames distinct. The start time itself is recorded at capture as its own field and must never be re-read from the id: a long project basename gets the id bounded at the tail, and the timestamp goes with it. The basename is lossy and is identity, not a container: never parse it as a cwd (the authoritative cwd lives in run-state.json, which is excluded); the container dimension stays empty. Whitelist: only chat-messages.json and chat-meta.json are captured (run-state.json, log.jsonl and in-flight *.tmp files are deliberately ignored), sealed whole-file as raw bytes, one full generation per changed pass. A transcript that does not read whole and validate as a JSON array skips its session for the pass: nothing is sealed, a bounded skip observation is recorded, and the run reports it. FREEBUFF_CONFIG_DIR replaces the whole base directory for every build and is therefore entry-wide: when set, the primary root reads the override value and the default-only dev/staging roots are not scanned; when unset, all three roots scan. message-history.json is a per-machine input log, not a session, and is not part of this capture. dimensions: none recorded (the artifacts carry no surface, tenant, container or status field).
harnesses.seal_source: upstream cli/src/utils/write-file-atomic.ts:8-39 — the transcript is written temp-then-rename in its own directory on every checkpoint (~5 s while a session is live), so a copy-only seal observes a complete generation and the source is never renamed or moved; a torn file the atomic write left behind is skipped, never half-sealed

harnesses.notes: Read-only dual-store adapter for the WorkBuddy desktop app (W1046): sqlite session metadata plus JSONL transcripts, one session id shared by both halves. The registry root is the projects/ directory; the sessions store is the sibling workbuddy.db, opened strictly as mode=ro (never immutable=1; a WAL store whose -shm sidecar is absent is read through a copied db, -wal and -shm trio in a temporary directory that is deleted after the read). Rows enumerate from the sessions table; a row with deleted_at IS NOT NULL is a tombstone: it exports a bare tombstone line that carries no row payload, so a session the source deleted is recorded as deleted while its earlier archived bytes stay in the archive. A live row without a matching *.jsonl transcript (a transport this machine does not hold local transcripts for, or the community-observed rows whose jsonl is gone) is a recognized session this build cannot archive: the scan names the difference as a gap and collect reports it and exits 3, never 0. The transcript walk globs only *.jsonl below projects/, excluding *.file-rollback.ndjson files and tool-results/ subdirectories by name; a session whose transcripts exist under more than one project slug is archived from the newest-mtime copy and the stale copies are named in the scan note. ~/.workbuddy/models.json is never opened or read. The reader handles nine top-level transcript types (session-meta, message, reasoning, function_call, function_call_result, file-history-snapshot, ai-title, summary, turn-metrics); the final two were measured on the sibling CodeBuddy CLI, which writes the same event core the desktop app uses.

harnesses.notes: Read-only transcript adapter for the CodeBuddy CLI (W1047), the sibling build of the WorkBuddy desktop app's cbc core: the two products write the same nine-type JSONL event core, and this source reuses the W1046 reader wholesale instead of forking a second one. The registry root is the projects/ directory, and the walk accepts both measured layouts — the flat projects/<session-id>.jsonl files and the projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl files — with only *.jsonl ever a transcript: the *.file-rollback.ndjson journals are excluded by name, subdirectories inside a project slug (the tool-results/ derivative cache) never hold transcripts, and any deeper nesting is unmeasured and skipped. The CLI keeps no sqlite session store, so there is no tombstone arm and no row-join: each transcript archives on its own file-name stem through the ordinary append-only jsonl reader, and the same session id in more than one location is archived from the newest-mtime copy with the stale copies named in the scan note. Because the file name is the only record that a session exists, a *.jsonl name the walk accepted whose metadata could not be read is a recognized session this build cannot archive: the scan names the difference as a gap and collect reports it and exits 3, never 0 — the transcripts-only counterpart of the desktop store's live-row-without-transcript rule. The reader handles the same nine top-level transcript types the desktop entry names; the CLI-only summary and turn-metrics lines were measured from this very source. ~/.codebuddy/history.jsonl is the declared machine log above, never a session.
